concepts.why: Patient has symmetric swelling of metacarpophalangeal joints, positive anti-SSA antibodies, and hilar lymphadenopathy on Chest CT, which are consistent with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
Patient has arthralgias, symmetric swelling of metacarpophalangeal joints, and ulcers on dorsal MCPs, which are consistent with Rheumatoid Arthritis.

Patient has hilar lymphadenopathy, interstitial thickening, and perilymphatic ground glass opacities on Chest CT, and worsening interstitial lung disease on follow-up Chest CT, which are consistent with Interstitial Lung Disease.
Patient has positive anti-SSA antibodies and orthokeratosis with rare lymphocytes at dermal/epidermal junction on skin biopsy, which are consistent with Sjögren's Syndrome.
Patient has ulcers on dorsal MCPs and diffuse vasculopathy with fibrin thrombi in deep dermal vessels on skin biopsy, which are consistent with Vasculitis.

Patient has overlapping features of different connective tissue diseases, including arthralgias, symmetric swelling of metacarpophalangeal joints, and positive anti-SSA antibodies, which are consistent with Mixed Connective Tissue Disease.

Patient has hilar lymphadenopathy, interstitial thickening, and perilymphatic ground glass opacities on Chest CT, and worsening interstitial lung disease on follow-up Chest CT, which are consistent with Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis.

Patient has symmetric swelling of metacarpophalangeal joints, ulcers on dorsal MCPs, and diffuse vasculopathy with fibrin thrombi in deep dermal vessels on skin biopsy, which are consistent with Systemic Sclerosis.

rationales.F01: Fatigue is a non-specific symptom that can be seen in many conditions.
rationales.F04: Symmetric swelling of metacarpophalangeal joints is more typical of Rheumatoid Arthritis.
rationales.F05: Dorsal MCP ulcers can be seen in several conditions, including Rheumatoid Arthritis and Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
rationales.F08: Anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies are highly specific for Sjögren's Syndrome and Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
rationales.F09: Hilar lymphadenopathy and interstitial lung disease can be seen in several conditions, including Systemic Lupus Erythematosus and Interstitial Lung Disease.
rationales.F10: Worsening interstitial lung disease is more typical of Interstitial Lung Disease and Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
rationales.F12: Skin biopsy findings are non-specific and can be seen in several conditions.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including symmetric joint swelling, lymphocytopenia, and elevated ferritin, along with the presence of anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies, are more consistent with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, which explains the decisive findings without strong contradiction.
